title: Chicken or Turkey Salad with Fat‑Free Dressing

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken or turkey salad is a dish made from boiled or roasted poultry, fresh vegetables and leafy greens, tossed with any fat‑free dressing (such as vinegar, lemon juice or non‑fat yogurt). The salad is high in protein, low in calories and suitable for diet‑focused eating.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken and turkey are among the most widely consumed sources of lean protein worldwide.
Fat‑free dressings keep the calorie count low while adding tangy flavor.
Athletes often include poultry salads in post‑workout meals for quick muscle recovery.
Leafy greens provide vitamin K, folate and other micronutrients.
Traditionally served cold, the salad can also be lightly warmed if preferred.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Poultry supplies complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low calorie density
items.content: The absence of fat in the dressing makes the dish ideal for weight management.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken and turkey contain niacin, vitamin B6 and B12, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: The salad provides iron, zinc and phosphorus, important for immunity and bone health.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Acidic fat‑free dressings (vinegar, lemon) improve nutrient absorption.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken or turkey.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Undercooked meat can harbor salmonella or campylobacter; ensure poultry is fully cooked.

items.title: Sodium in ready‑made dressings
items.content: Certain fat‑free dressings are high in salt; people with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Digestive discomfort from excess fiber
items.content: Large amounts of raw vegetables may cause gas in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled as a main dish or side. It pairs well with whole‑grain breads, legumes, or can be wrapped in a flatbread. For the dressing, mix non‑fat yogurt, lemon juice, mustard and herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Store the dressing separately to maintain crispness of the greens.
